title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: Fig. 2h-j; Extended Data Fig. 3; Methods 'Optogenetics experiments with 3D joint kinematics'; Genotypes table (PDF p. 29)
quote: DNg100 activation produced forward walking on the ball, but at a lower speed than is typical of wild-type flies
mapping_basis: Paper uses the MANC type name DNg100 (also notes it is BDN2); kit synonyms map BDN2 to DNg100 and the kit row BDN2-splitGal4 has the same AD/DBD (VT058557 x R85F12) as the genotype used.
stimulation: 638 nm laser, 1200 Hz, 30% duty cycle, focused at front left body-coxa joint; 0.03, 0.09 and 0.33 mW/mm2; 5 s stim-on; strongest condition 0.33 mW/mm2
sensory_condition: decapitated, de-winged, tethered on air-supported spherical treadmill
frequency_note: L1 step frequency read approximately from Fig. 2j medians: ~3.5 Hz (0.03), ~5.1 Hz (0.09), ~5.6 Hz (0.33 mW/mm2); frequency increased with laser intensity (paired t-tests p=0.032 low-medium, 0.042 low-high). Value is from the strongest condition, read off the plot.
coordination_notes: Generally tetrapod coordination pattern (Methods; Extended Data Fig. 3 stance-count and inter-leg phase plots for all six legs).
penetrance: Forward velocity rose from ~0 at stim onset at all three intensities (Fig. 2i, mean over flies); walking slower than typical wild-type
n_flies_note: n=7 flies, 8 trials per fly per intensity
notes: Walking was induced from rest in headless flies, so effect_on_walking is 'not_assessed' (section 3: that field is for flies already walking); forward velocity and step frequency increased with laser intensity. Fly age 10-12 days. Line expression shown only as a confocal image; off-target labelling not described. Simulation panels (Fig. 2a-g, Fig. 1e) not used.

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
